indications: gout prophylaxis; hyperuricemia; prevention of tumor lysis syndrome
standard_dose: 100-300 mg daily initially and titrated by urate target and renal function
contraindications_relative: renal impairment; HLA-B*58:01 risk populations; hepatic impairment
adverse_effects: rash; gastrointestinal upset; hepatotoxicity; severe cutaneous adverse reactions
major_interactions: azathioprine; mercaptopurine; warfarin
half_life: allopurinol 1-2 h; oxypurinol 15 h or longer

mechanism_of_action: Mu-opioid receptor agonist producing central analgesia
indications: moderate to severe pain; acute pulmonary edema in selected settings
standard_dose: highly individualized; commonly 5-10 mg orally every 4 h for immediate-release in opioid-naive adults
contraindications_absolute: significant respiratory depression; acute severe bronchial asthma without monitoring; paralytic ileus
contraindications_relative: head injury; renal impairment; hepatic impairment; concomitant sedatives
adverse_effects: constipation; nausea; sedation; respiratory depression; pruritus
major_interactions: benzodiazepines; alcohol; other CNS depressants

mechanism_of_action: Central analgesic and antipyretic action, likely involving cyclooxygenase modulation in the CNS
indications: pain; fever
standard_dose: 500-1000 mg every 4-6 h; usual adult max 4 g/day
contraindications_absolute: severe hypersensitivity; severe acute hepatocellular failure
contraindications_relative: chronic liver disease; alcohol misuse; low body weight; malnutrition
adverse_effects: usually well tolerated; hepatotoxicity in overdose; rash rare
major_interactions: alcohol; warfarin with prolonged regular use; enzyme inducers
metabolism: hepatic glucuronidation and sulfation; minor CYP2E1 pathway

mechanism_of_action: Blocks voltage-gated sodium channels and reduces repetitive neuronal firing
indications: focal seizures; trigeminal neuralgia; bipolar disorder in selected patients
standard_dose: 200 mg 1-2 times daily initially, titrated gradually
contraindications_absolute: bone marrow depression; concomitant MAOI use; hypersensitivity to carbamazepine or tricyclic compounds
contraindications_relative: hepatic impairment; cardiac conduction disease; HLA-B*1502 or HLA-A*3101 risk populations
adverse_effects: dizziness; diplopia; ataxia; hyponatremia; rash; agranulocytosis rare
major_interactions: oral contraceptives; warfarin; many antiepileptics; macrolides; azoles
half_life: initially 25-65 h, then 12-17 h with autoinduction

mechanism_of_action: Antagonist at dopamine D2 and serotonin 5-HT2 receptors with additional receptor effects
indications: schizophrenia; bipolar disorder; agitation depending on formulation
standard_dose: 5-20 mg daily
contraindications_relative: diabetes mellitus; obesity; dyslipidemia; elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis
adverse_effects: weight gain; sedation; metabolic syndrome; anticholinergic effects; orthostatic hypotension
major_interactions: CNS depressants; smoking can lower levels; fluvoxamine can increase levels

mechanism_of_action: Positive allosteric modulator of the GABA-A receptor
indications: anxiety; status epilepticus; alcohol withdrawal; muscle spasm
standard_dose: 2-10 mg 1-4 times daily depending on indication
contraindications_absolute: myasthenia gravis; severe respiratory insufficiency; sleep apnea syndrome; severe hepatic insufficiency
contraindications_relative: elderly patients; substance misuse; concomitant opioids; depression
adverse_effects: sedation; impaired coordination; confusion; respiratory depression; dependence
major_interactions: opioids; alcohol; other CNS depressants; CYP inhibitors

mechanism_of_action: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor
indications: major depressive disorder; obsessive-compulsive disorder; panic disorder; bulimia nervosa
standard_dose: 20-60 mg once daily depending on indication
contraindications_relative: bipolar disorder; seizure disorders; QT prolongation risk; hepatic impairment
adverse_effects: nausea; insomnia; anxiety; sexual dysfunction; serotonin syndrome; hyponatremia
major_interactions: MAO inhibitors; linezolid; tramadol; warfarin; tamoxifen

mechanism_of_action: Inhibits dopamine and norepinephrine reuptake in the CNS
indications: attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder; narcolepsy
standard_dose: formulation-dependent; commonly 5-10 mg once or twice daily initially
contraindications_absolute: concomitant MAOI use; glaucoma; marked anxiety or agitation; hypersensitivity
contraindications_relative: hypertension; structural cardiac disease; tic disorders; substance misuse risk
adverse_effects: insomnia; decreased appetite; tachycardia; anxiety; growth suppression in children
major_interactions: MAO inhibitors; antihypertensives; other sympathomimetics

mechanism_of_action: Selective beta-2 adrenergic receptor agonist causing bronchodilation
indications: acute bronchospasm; asthma; COPD symptom relief; exercise-induced bronchospasm prevention
routes_of_administration: inhalation; oral; intravenous depending on formulation
standard_dose: 100-200 micrograms by inhalation as needed
contraindications_relative: tachyarrhythmias; ischemic heart disease; hyperthyroidism; hypokalemia risk
adverse_effects: tremor; tachycardia; palpitations; hypokalemia; nervousness
major_interactions: nonselective beta blockers; diuretics; MAO inhibitors and sympathomimetics

mechanism_of_action: Long-acting muscarinic receptor antagonist causing bronchodilation
indications: COPD maintenance therapy; asthma add-on maintenance therapy
standard_dose: 1 inhaled dose once daily depending on device and formulation
contraindications_absolute: hypersensitivity to tiotropium or atropine-like compounds
contraindications_relative: narrow-angle glaucoma; urinary retention; prostatic hyperplasia
adverse_effects: dry mouth; constipation; urinary retention; blurred vision
major_interactions: other anticholinergics

mechanism_of_action: Peripheral H1 antihistamine receptor antagonist
indications: allergic rhinitis; urticaria
standard_dose: 10 mg once daily
contraindications_relative: hepatic impairment
adverse_effects: headache; dry mouth; mild somnolence; fatigue
major_interactions: CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 inhibitors

mechanism_of_action: Prostaglandin F2alpha analogue that increases uveoscleral aqueous humor outflow
indications: open-angle glaucoma; ocular hypertension
standard_dose: 1 drop in the affected eye once daily in the evening
contraindications_relative: uveitis; herpetic keratitis history; aphakia or macular edema risk
adverse_effects: conjunctival hyperemia; iris pigmentation; eyelash growth; ocular irritation
major_interactions: other prostaglandin analogues
half_life: about 17 min in plasma; ocular effect much longer

english_name: ethyl esters of iodised fatty acids
